voice_instructions: Measured, quiet, a little hushed — calm and unhurried, but with a touch more forward energy than a long documentary; the cold voice of something that read the whole file. Never sensational. Small pauses.

beats.vo: The Atlantic, May nineteen sixty-eight. The nuclear submarine Scorpion was heading home to Norfolk, Virginia.
Ninety-nine men were aboard. Her last message came on May twenty-first. She was due on the twenty-seventh. She never arrived.
The search went on for months. In the Azores, deep-diving gear was readied to help.
In late October, the research ship Mizar found her, southwest of the Azores, almost two miles down.
A Navy court of inquiry said the certain cause could not be ascertained. An explosion, a torpedo, a battery fault: all remain theories.
